lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm inquiring about my child Alex. They live at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to ask a few more questions about Alex to determine eligibility.

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of their exact age at the moment - they're somewhere between 15 and 19. Is that alright?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know they're between 15 and 19. The exact age is important because different rules apply at age 16 and beyond, so I do need to narrow this down a bit.

**Can you confirm whether Alex is under 16, or 16 or over?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm really sorry, I honestly can't say for certain whether they're under or over 16. I know that sounds odd, but that's just my situation right now. Is there a way to work with that, or do you absolutely need the exact age?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand your situation. Let me explain why the age matters, as it will help clarify what we need to determine:

- **Under 16**: A child under 16 generally qualifies for Child Benefit (subject to other conditions)
- **16 or over**: A young person aged 16-19 can still qualify, but only if they're in approved education or training

Since Alex is somewhere between 15 and 19, there are different possible outcomes depending on their actual age. However, I can work with this uncertainty to some extent.

Let me ask this: **Is Alex currently in any form of education or training?** (This could include school, college, certain approved training programs, etc.)

This will help me assess eligibility across the possible age scenarios.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me explain how this affects eligibility:

Given that Alex is between 15 and 19 years old and is **not** currently in education or training, here's the situation:

- **If Alex is under 16**: They would generally be eligible for Child Benefit
- **If Alex is 16 or over**: They would **not** be eligible for Child Benefit, because young people aged 16-19 must be in approved education or training to qualify

Since you're uncertain whether Alex is under or over 16, and this is the critical factor that determines eligibility, I cannot make a definitive determination either way.

Before I provide my assessment, let me ask a couple more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex? That is, do you provide for them and they live with you full-time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives with me full-time and I'm responsible for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Now let me ask about your residency status, as this is also relevant for Child Benefit eligibility:

**Are you currently living in the UK, and do you have the right to reside here?** (For example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, or another immigration status that gives you the right to live in the UK?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm in Birmingham, and yes, I have the right to live here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me also check one more thing:

**Are you the only person responsible for Alex, or is there anyone else (such as another parent or guardian) who might also be claiming or intending to claim Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's no one else claiming Child Benefit for Alex. I'm the only one.
